tip: On a 2-on-1, read the lone defenceman. If they take you, the pass is open; if they sag to the pass, take it yourself.
why: The lone defender can only take one threat. Reading which one they commit to tells you whether to shoot or pass.

interaction.prompt: 2-on-1, you're carrying wide into the zone. Where do you go with the puck?

mc.stem: 2-on-1 off the rush. You're carrying wide into the zone with a trailer cutting to the back door. What's your best read?
opts: Slide it across to the trailing centre
Chip it in deep and chase

feedback.right: Yes. The D committed to you, so the back door is wide open. Move it across.
feedback.wrong: The D stepped to you, so forcing a shot or driving in lets the one defender win. The trailer was the open man.

routes.outcome: The D stayed on you — the centre is alone at the back door.
The D had stepped to you — the trailer was open. Now here's the flip: the D sags to the trailer instead.

interaction.prompt: The pass is on your tape at the back door and the goalie is sliding across. Tap where you shoot.

feedback.right: Yes — shoot into the open far side before the goalie recovers.
feedback.wrong: The goalie is sliding across to cover the near side; the open net is the far side, away from where they're moving.

interaction.prompt: The D broke it up. On a 2-on-1 where the D takes the carrier, what should you have done?

mc.stem: The D took you and broke up the play. On a 2-on-1 when the lone D commits to the puck carrier, the right read is:

feedback.right: Right — when the D takes you, the trailer is the open man.
feedback.wrong: When the D commits to you, forcing your own shot plays into the one defender. The trailer is open.
